question: As a nurse, what is the main reason you need access to healthcare data?

options.A: Writing research papers for medical journals
options.B: Retrieving, viewing, and sharing patient health information
options.D: Printing out daily hospital financial reports

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare data access simply means being able to pull up, check, and share patient details so you can give them the best care possible. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is having quick access to patient data so important for safe nursing?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for physical patient charts
options.B: It allows nurses to diagnose complex diseases independently
options.C: It reduces the total number of hospital admission days
options.D: It prevents medical errors and delayed treatments

explanation: You got it! When you can check vital records and notes fast, you make safer decisions and avoid delays that could harm your patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Under which data category do a patient's vital signs and lab results fall?
explanation: Well done! Vital signs, nursing notes, and lab reports are all direct measures of a patient's health status, which makes them clinical data. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: How would you best describe an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: An online social network for doctors and nurses
options.B: A private database strictly for hospital billing officers
options.C: A physical filing cabinet locked in the records department
options.D: A digital version of paper charts centralizing patient data

explanation: Exactly! Think of an EHR as the modern, digital upgrade to the old paper folder, keeping all a patient's health details in one easy-to-reach place. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which regulation protects data privacy and security here in Nigeria?
explanation: Correct! The Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) is the legal rulebook that guides how sensitive information is kept safe in our country. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a nurse's biggest ethical duty when it comes to a patient's health details?

options.A: Sharing medical history with any inquiring family member
options.B: Publishing interesting case studies on social media
options.C: Maintaining strict confidentiality at all times
options.D: Displaying patient diagnosis charts in public waiting areas

explanation: Spot on! Patient trust is sacred. We always keep patient information private and never gossip about it outside professional spaces. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is a major security violation when using hospital computers?

options.A: Sharing personal login credentials with a colleague
options.B: Reading patient notes assigned to your own ward
options.C: Reporting a broken computer screen to IT support
options.D: Logging out of the terminal when leaving the desk

explanation: You got it! Never share your password. If someone else logs in with your details, any mistakes they make will trace right back to you. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: You just finished checking lab results on a nursing station computer and an emergency pops up in Room 4. What should you do?

options.A: Leave the screen open so the next nurse can see the results
options.B: Cover the monitor with a piece of paper and run away
options.C: Ask a passing cleaner to watch the computer screen
options.D: Log out of the computer session immediately before leaving

explanation: Brilliant! Always hit that logout button before rushing off. It takes two seconds and keeps patient data safe from prying eyes. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: How do nurses typically interact with patient health records during a shift?

options.A: They only read information entered by medical doctors
options.B: They both input new data and retrieve information for care
options.C: Ones in management handle billing while floor nurses write notes
options.D: They archive paper files at the end of each calendar month

explanation: Spot on! Nurses wear two hats here: you type in fresh observations as they happen, and you read past records to guide your care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is clear, accurate nursing documentation so important for the rest of the team?

options.A: It ensures reliable data is available for medical rounds and handovers
options.B: It allows hospital accountants to calculate staff salary bonuses
options.C: It guarantees that patients will be discharged within twenty-four hours
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal communication among workers

explanation: Correct! Good notes mean smooth handovers. When the next shift takes over, they won't have to guess what happened to your patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge for digital health records in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.D: Heavy reliance on paper-based filing systems

explanation: You nailed it! Blazing fast internet is definitely not something Nigerian hospitals struggle with having *too much* of! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is one of the biggest risks of sticking strictly to paper-based health records?

options.A: They require expensive electricity generators to remain readable
options.B: They are easily damaged, lost, or affected by illegible handwriting
options.C: They automatically update themselves when lab results are ready
options.D: They provide instant access to records across multiple distant branches

explanation: Spot on! Paper can easily get torn, soaked, misplaced, or written in handwriting that looks like chicken scratch! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)
